results.name: Custom Reports in Clio Manage
results.title: Custom Reports in Clio Manage
results.body:
Reports in Clio Manage are designed to help your law firm track deliverables and get insights into all aspects of how the firm is performing. Classic reports in Clio Manage provide ready-to-use reports for common use cases along with the ability to customize the reports to highlight specific insights from the data. Refer to Clio Manage Reports, Presets, and History to learn more about these reports.

For nuanced reporting needs, Clio Manage also offers the ability to create custom reports. With custom reports you have access to more data in Clio Manage and additional control of filter functionality.

Note: The Custom reports feature is currently in and is being gradually released over the coming weeks. If you do not see it in your account yet, it will become available to you soon.

 

Generate custom reports in Clio Manage

Note: Firms in the US on Signature and Elite plans and firms in Canada on Advanced or Expand plans can create custom reports. Other users can select any of the pre-built Clio reports and then refine them (step 2).

Step 1: Create a new custom report

  1. In Clio Manage, go to the main Reports tab, then select the Reports tab.

  2. Click Create new custom report.

    Note: If you want to create a new report that is similar to an existing report, you can duplicate an existing report by clicking the More icon (three horizontal dots) on any of the existing cards, then clicking Duplicate and customize.

    If your firm uses Clio's AI features, you can use the prompt window to describe the report you need with natural language. When you submit the prompt, Clio's AI will preselect relevant fields and calculations to get you started. You can then make adjustments by adding or deleting fields before creating your report. Learn how to use Clio's AI features to generate reports in Clio Manage.

  3. Add the report Name, Description, and Category.
  4. Select your dataset. For information on the available datasets and their descriptions, refer to Understand available datasets.

  5. Add the fields and calculations to include in your report.

    • As you select fields and calculations, a preview of your report will be displayed (with sample data).
    Tip: The fields and calculations you select will be the descriptive column headers (or column name) in the data sheet. Click the question mark next to any field or calculation for a basic description of the data.
  6. Once you have selected all fields and calculations to include in the report, click Create report.

To find the created report at a later time, find it in your Custom tab.

Tip: Common, ready-to-use reports are also available. Find them in the Clio tab in the Reports section.

Step 2: Refine the custom report

Once you create a report, you can refine it by rearranging the columns, filtering the data, and grouping data.

Note: You can filter and group your data on the standard Clio fields, but not on any custom fields.
  • Click Columns to open the columns pane. Drag and drop the columns to rearrange them on the report. Use the eye icon for a column name to show or hide the column from view. Your report will update as you make changes to the columns.
  • Click Filters to open the filters pane. When you first open this pane, a default date filter with values for the previous month will be applied. Click Add filter to remove this pre-set date filter and choose your own date range. Choose the field to filter on, then choose the condition. Your report will update as you add and remove filters or change filter conditions. You can add as many filters as you like.
  • Click Groups to open the groups pane. You can currently choose up to two levels to group by. Click Apply to change the order of the row grouping in your report, or Apply and close to do the same and close the groups pane. Your report now also includes additional rows that provide summary information for your groupings.
  • For relevant reports, click Currency to select the currency for your report.

If you anticipate needing this report again in the future, along with the filters and groupings applied, you can save it as a Report view.

Note: Firms in the US on Signature or Elite plans and firms in Canada on Advanced and Expand plans can save as many report views as they like. Those on Core plans (US) or Essentials plans (Canada) can save up to five report views per Clio report.
  1. Click Save report view.
  2. Add a short and descriptive name.
  3. Click Save report view.

This will save the report that you generated in step 1 including the refinements you made in step 2 for later use. The breadcrumb indicates the sequential nature of how this particular report view is saved. The Custom Report represents the report you generated in step 1 while the Report View includes the refinements you made in step 2 (rearranging, filtering, and grouping). You can find both your Reports and your Report views in their respective sections in the Reports tab.

View, edit, export, or delete custom reports and report views

If you are a Primary subscriber, Administrator, or have Report role permissions, you can view the custom reports and report views you created, as well as those created by any other user in Clio Manage.

Tip: Search by name or use the filter to quickly find a specific custom report.
Card view Table view
  • Click Preview on the report to view a summary of the report.
  • Click on the name of the report to view more details. Each of the report’s subtabs provide information about the report.
    • Report: View information about the report itself, including a summary of key metrics gleaned from the report, the columns of the report and how they are arranged, filters applied, and groupings applied.
    • Report views: See a list of all unique views created from the original report.
    • History: This tab shows a list of previous report exports along with the user who exported the report, the time of export, and the export format. You can also download the specific copy of that export.
  • Click on the more icon (the three horizontal dots) to do any of the following: Edit report, Export report, Duplicate and customize the report, or Delete report.

  • Click on the name of the report to view more details. Each of the report’s subtabs provide information about the report.

  • Click on the edit (pencil) icon to edit the report.

You can access report views from the following locations.

  2. Scroll down to the Report views section.

    Tip: Search by name or use the filter to quickly find a specific report view.
  3. Find, then click the name of the report view to open and view details about it. Each of the report view’s subtabs provide information about the report.
    • Report views: View information about the report view itself, including a summary of key metrics gleaned from the report view, the columns of the report and how they are arranged, filters applied, and groupings applied

  2. Click the name of a report to open and view it.
  3. Click the Report views subtab.
  4. Click the name of the report view to open and view it.

 

Schedule report views

To help you to keep up to date with your firm’s metrics and make insightful business decisions, you can schedule generating report views.

Note: Users on Core and higher plans (US) or Essentials and higher plans (Canada) have the ability to schedule reports. Essentials (US) or Core (Canada) users can allow personal notifications when a scheduled report is generated, whereas Signature and Elite (US) or Advanced and Expand users (Canada) can send notifications to themselves and other users in the firm when a scheduled report is generated.
  1. In Clio Manage, go to the main Reports tab. Ensure the Reports tab is selected.
  2. Scroll down to the Report views table and click Add schedule for the relevant report view. You can also click Schedule when viewing a report view.
    • If you previously scheduled this report, click on Daily/Weekly/Monthly to open the modal to edit the schedule
  3. Add the required details including how often to generate the report, the time at which to generate the report, the start date, who to notify, and the report format.
  4. Click Save schedule.

To delete a schedule, click the Daily, Weekly, or Monthly link for the report view, then Remove schedule.

 

Understand available datasets

To streamline the process of creating custom reports, Clio Manage organizes available data into logical datasets that contain related data. This makes it easier to find the specific data fields you need to answer questions related to particular topics.

When you generate a report, you will be able to choose a particular dataset and you can view the various fields and calculations available along with their descriptions to help you choose the most appropriate data to include in your report.

 

Account transactions dataset

The Account Transactions dataset gives you access to Clio Manage data related to your operating and trust transactions along with information related to transaction dates, bills, trust requests, matters (both standard and select custom fields), and contacts (both standard and select custom fields), allowing you to answer questions at the meeting point of the data. Custom fields that are of the type Contact select, Matter select, or Text (Multi-line) are not available for use in custom reports.

You can refer to the previous examples for the Bills and Time entry productivity datasets to understand how to leverage any dataset to create relevant reports in order to make data-driven decisions for your firm.

 

Bills dataset

The Bills dataset gives you access to Clio Manage data related to bills, payments, and balances, along with information related to matters (both standard and select custom fields), contacts (both standard and select custom fields), and bill dates, allowing you to answer questions at the meeting point of the data. Custom fields that are of the type Contact select, Matter select, or Text (Multi-line) are not available for use in custom reports. The following example scenario can help you understand how to gain insight into your firm’s billing.

Bills report example

Imagine you need insight into the amounts you billed over the course of the last two years, along with information about how much you collected on these bills vs how much remains unpaid. You also want to know how these amounts were different for matters with different practice areas. Since the bills dataset comprises the information you require, you can generate a report to provide you with these insights.

When you generate a report, you can select the Practice area and Bill due year fields and the Payment total and Bill balance total calculations.

Then, use the filters and columns to to refine the report (step 2) for your specific question. In the current example, you might do the following:

  • Click Filters and adjust the time period to include data from the last two years.
    • Add a filter where you set the Bill due at date value to a period spanning the last two years.
  • Use the grouping function to group by Bill due year, then by Practice area.
Tip: Reverse these fields if you are interested in understanding how billings are affected by practice areas and subsequently you want to see how that changes over the two-year period.

For this particular example, you can also arrange the columns to provide the same information you obtain using the grouping function. You can arrange the columns so that the table is organized first by Bill due at year (as the first column), then Practice area (as the second column) to organize billings and payments in the table list.

 

Calendar entries dataset

The Calendar entries dataset gives you access to Clio Manage data related to your calendar entries, including the calendar events' titles, descriptions, dates, times, and locations, the total number of calendar events and the total duration of the events, various matter fields for the matters that are related to the calendar entries (including select matter custom fields), various contact fields for the contacts associated with the calendar entries (including select contact custom fields), and more. Matter and contact custom fields that are of the type Contact select, Matter select, or Text (Multi-line) are not available for use in custom reports. This dataset allows you to gain insights about your how your firm members plan and attend meetings and other scheduled events.

You can refer to the previous examples for the Bills and Time entry productivity datasets to understand how to leverage any dataset to create relevant reports in order to make data-driven decisions for your firm.

 

Fee allocation dataset

The Fee allocation dataset gives you access to data on how collected fees are split among the users assigned to a matter's Originating Lawyer, Responsible Lawyer, and Responsible Staff roles, based on the allocations set in the firm's fee allocation settings or fee allocation settings applied to matters. This dataset allows you to distinguishes between the firm member who earned fees for their work (fee earner) and firms users who may be credited with a share of the earned fees as part of firm policies. For example, matters where a firm member is added as the originating attorney may be credited a certain percentage of the fees earned by the responsible attorney on that matter. The dataset provides access to Clio Manage data related to allocation roles and firm members listed in allocation settings, allocation percentages, fee earner information, collected time, and allocated amounts.

 

Online payments dataset

The Clio Payments dataset gives you access to Clio Payments transaction data, including charges, refunds, chargebacks, reinstatements, fees, surcharges, and payout dates, along with information related to clients, and bank accounts, allowing you to answer questions at the meeting point of the data.

You can refer to the previous examples for the Bills and Time entry productivity datasets to understand how to leverage any dataset to create relevant reports in order to make data-driven decisions for your firm.

 

Matters dataset

The Matters dataset gives you access to Clio Manage data related to your matters, including matter open and close dates and the stage of the matter, matter bill information, firm members working on matters, select matter custom fields and more. The dataset also provides contact information related to your matters (both standard and select custom contact fields), allowing you to gain deep insights related to your firm's matters. Custom fields that are of the type Contact select, Matter select, or Text (Multi-line) are not available for use in custom reports.

You can refer to the previous examples for the Bills and Time entry productivity datasets to understand how to leverage any dataset to create relevant reports in order to make data-driven decisions for your firm.

 

Payments & credit notes dataset

The Payment & Credit Notes dataset gives you access to Clio Manage data related to collected and credited monetary values and hours, etc., along with information related to matters (both standard and select custom fields), contacts (both standard and select custom fields), payment and bill dates, and firm users allowing you to answer questions at the meeting point of the data. Custom fields that are of the type Contact select, Matter select, or Text (Multi-line) are not available for use in custom reports.

You can refer to the previous examples for the Bills and Time entry productivity datasets to understand how to leverage any dataset to create relevant reports in order to make data-driven decisions for your firm.

 

Time entry productivity dataset

The Time entry productivity dataset gives you access to Clio Manage data related to non-billable, billable, billed, unbilled, and tracked hours, along with information related to activity dates, matters (both standard and select custom fields), contacts (both standard and select custom fields), and firm users to answer questions at the meeting point of the data. Custom fields that are of the type Contact select, Matter select, or Text (Multi-line) are not available for use in custom reports. The following example scenario can help you understand how to gain insight into your firm’s productivity and some of the factors that may affect productivity.

Time entry productivity report example
  1. You want to determine how productive different members are at your firm in order to offer development opportunities where it may be needed.
  2. You want to determine which matter types or practice areas are more lucrative for your firm.

Since the Time entry productivity dataset comprises the information you require, you can generate a report to provide you with these insights.

When you generate a report, you can select the Matter description, Practice area, and User full name fields and the Billed hours value, Unbilled hours value, and Utilization rate calculations. Then, use the filters and columns to refine the report for your specific question. In the current example, you might do the following:

  • Click Filters and adjust the time period to include data from the previous quarter to get a representative time range to answer your questions.
    • Click Filter, then select the activity date for Last quarter.
  • To answer the first question, use the grouping function to group by User full name to view the Billed hours value, Unbilled hours value, and Utilization rate per firm user. You can save this report view if you are interested in referring to it again.
  • To answer the second question, change the grouping to group by Matter description or Practice area, whichever option you find the most relevant. The Practice area field has a limited number of categories, making grouping easy, but if your firm uses consistent Matter descriptions, this field may also be useful in this example. Once again, you can save this report view if you are interested in referring to it again.

results.body:
Reports in Clio Manage are designed to help your law firm track deliverables and get insights into all aspects of how the firm is performing. Revenue reports provide a comprehensive overview of your firm's financial performance by showing total collected activities and taxes, amounts generated by each originating attorney, and amounts each firm user has billed and collected for each matter. In each section below, a summary of a particular revenue report in Clio Manage is provided, along with details of the information the report offers.

Note: Every report in Clio is unique in the criteria it uses to calculate financial data. This means that comparing different types of reports is not recommended. Not all reports are available for all Clio subscription plans. Learn more about reports available on your subscription plan and upgrading your plan here.
Tip: For instructions about generating reports, creating reports presets (i.e., saving the filters used to generate a report), scheduling automated report generation, and viewing a history of generated reports, refer to Generate Reports, Presets, and History.

Revenue report

The revenue report is designed to give firms a detailed overview of unbilled, billed, and collected time and expense activities. This report also includes taxes, credit notes, discounted time, and discounted expenses by matter. You can use this report to help quantify key performance metrics on a per user, per client, and per matter basis.

Note: By default, partial payments and credit notes applied to invoices are allocated proportionally across all line items. If you change this setting to allocate partial payments and credit notes in a different way, the following columns will be calculated depending on the selected allocation method: Collected time, Collected expense, Collected tax 1, and Collected tax 2. Learn more about the reports allocation setting here.

When generated, the Web and PDF versions of the report includes the following columns:

Matter

This column lists the matter identifier. 

Location

This column shows the value entered in the Location field for a matter.  

Unbilled time

This column shows the monetary value of unbilled time entries for the matter. Unbilled time entries are time entries that are not generated on any approved bills, including time entries that are not on a bill and time entries that are on bills in draft or bills pending approval.

Unbilled hours

This column shows unbilled time entry hours for the matter. Unbilled time entries are those that do not yet appear on any approved bills, i.e., time entries that are either not on a bill or on a bill in a draft state or pending approval.

Unbilled expense

This column shows the monetary value of unbilled expense entries for the matter. Unbilled expense entries are expenses that are not generated on any approved bills, including expenses that are not on a bill and expenses that are on bills in draft or bills pending approval.

Billed time

This column shows the monetary value of billed time entries for the matter. Billed time entries are time entries on approved bills.

Billed hours

This column shows billed time entry hours for the matter. Billed time entries are time entries on approved bills.

Billed expense

This column shows the dollar value of billed expense entries for the matter. Billed expense entries are expenses on approved bills.

Billed tax 1

This column shows the dollar value of your first tax on billed activities for the matter. Billed activities are billable time and expense entries on approved bills.

Billed tax 2

This column shows the dollar value of your second tax on billed activities for the matter. Billed activities are billable time and expense entries on approved bills.

Discounted time

This column shows the dollar value of billed time entries for the matter that had discounts applied to them. Billed time entries are time entries on approved bills.

Discounted expense

This column shows the dollar value of billed expense entries for the matter that had discounts applied to them. Billed expense entries are expenses on approved bills.

Credit notes

This column shows the dollar value of billed activities for the matter that had credit notes applied to them. Billed activities are time and expense entries on approved bills.

Collected time

This column shows the dollar value of billed time entries on generated bills that have been paid. If a partial payment was applied to a bill with time entries, the payment will be evenly applied across the Collected time, Collected expense, Collected tax, and Collected tax 2 columns. 

Collected expense

This column shows the dollar value of billed expense entries on generated bills that have been paid. If a partial payment was applied to a bill with expenses, the payment will be evenly applied across the Collected time, Collected expense, Collected tax 1, and Collected tax 2 columns.

Collected tax 1

This column shows the dollar value of your first tax on billed activities on generated bills that have been paid. If a partial payment was applied to a bill, the payment will be evenly applied across the Collected time, Collected expense, Collected tax 1, and Collected tax 2 columns.

Collected tax 2

This column shows the dollar value of your second tax on billed activities on generated bills that have been paid. If a partial payment was applied to a bill, the payment will be evenly applied across the Collected time, Collected expense, Collected tax 1, and Collected tax 2 columns.

Collected uncategorized

This column refers to collected money that is not attached to any matter or client.

Client total

This total refers to the total of each column for all of the client's matters. 

Summary information and totals are displayed at the bottom of the report.

No client/No practice area

This section will appear at the bottom of the report if you have revenue that is not attached to any client or practice area. The heading of the section (No Client vs No Practice Area) will depend on whether you grouped your results by client or practice area when you selected your options for generating the report.

Clio Scheduler payments

This section will appear at the bottom of the report and shows revenue for payments collected through Clio Scheduler appointments.

Total

The final line of the report provides the grand totals of all columns.

Reports in CSV and Excel format have the same columns as the Web and PDF reports along with some additional columns.

Client

Since the reports in CSV and Excel format are not grouped by client or practice area, this column shows the client name for the matter.

Practice Area

Since the reports in CSV and Excel format are not grouped by client or practice area, this column shows the practice area for the matter.

Matter Description

The description of the matter.

Responsible Attorney

The name of the Attorney assigned as responsible for the Matter.

Billed Interest

The monetary value of interest on overdue (approved) bills.

Collected Interest

The monetary value of interest collected on overdue bills.

It is useful to understand the details about which information is included in or excluded from the report depending on the date range selected when generating the report.

Expense and time entries have more than one date associated with it. For example, an entry has a date of creation, i.e. the date the entry was recorded in Clio, and the date that a bill was issued for the entry. These entries are included or excluded based on the following rules:

  • Unbilled information will be included if the date the entry was created falls within the date range selected when generating the report.
  • Billed information will be included if the bill issue date for that entry falls within the date range selected when generating the report.
  • Collected amounts and information will be included if the payment date falls within the date range selected when generating the report.

Credit notes appear on the report if the date the credit note was created falls within the date range selected when generating the report.

Originating attorney revenue report

The originating attorney revenue report is designed to help firms visualize and quantify how much revenue each attorney in the firm has brought in. This report includes taxes, interest, fees, and collected time and expense activities.

Note: This report only reflects the Originating Lawyer set in a matter's Matter Details section. It does not reflect the role allocations, percentages, or additional users set in the firm's fee allocation settings or fee allocation settings applied to the matter. To report on fee allocation that includes those, use the Fee allocation dataset in Custom Reports.

Note: By default, partial payments and credit notes applied to invoices are allocated proportionally across all line items. If you change this setting to allocate partial payments and credit notes in a different way, the following columns will be calculated depending on the selected allocation method: Collected time, Collected expense, Collected tax, and Collected tax 2. Learn more about the reports allocation setting here.

When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Attorney

This column lists the firm user who is designated as the originating attorney on a matter.

Collected time

This column shows the total value of the originating attorney's time entries on bills that have been paid. 

Collected expense

This column shows the total value of the originating attorney's expense entries on bills that have been paid. 

Collected interest

This column shows the total value of the interest on bills that have been paid for the originating attorney on the matter. 

Collected tax

This column shows the total value of the first tax on bills that have been paid for the originating attorney on the matter. 

Collected secondary tax

This column shows the total value of the second tax on bills that have been paid for the originating attorney on the matter. 

Grand total

This total summarizes the total collected amounts for each column for this originating attorney.

 

Fee allocation report

The fee allocation report is designed to give firms a detailed view of time and expenses each firm user has billed and collected for each matter. This report also includes accounts receivables and credit notes. You can use this report to determine your firm’s bonus payout to attorneys.

Note: This report only reflects the Originating Lawyer set in a matter's Matter Details section. It does not reflect the role allocations, percentages, or additional users set in the firm's fee allocation settings or fee allocation settings applied to the matter. To report on fee allocation that includes those, use the Fee allocation dataset in Custom Reports or use the Clio-built Fee allocation report in the Clio tab of Custom Report.

Note: By default, partial payments and credit notes applied to invoices are allocated proportionally across all line items. If you change this setting to allocate partial payments and credit notes in a different way, the columns listed below will be calculated depending on the selected allocation method. Learn more about the reports allocation setting here.

  • Billed time collected
  • Billing time outstanding
  • Expense amount collected (CSV only)
  • Expense amount outstanding (CSV only)
  • Primary tax collected (CSV only)
  • Primary tax outstanding (CSV only)
  • Secondary tax collected (CSV only)
  • Secondary tax outstanding (CSV only)

When generated, this report includes the following categories:

User

This column lists the firm user who created the activity entry. In the Web report, the report is organized into user sections.

Matter

This column lists the matter for which a firm user has billed and collected time and/or expenses. In the Web report, you can click on the matter to navigate to it. Use your browser’s back button to return to the report from the matter.

Client

This column lists the client for each matter. In the Web report, you can click on the client name to navigate to their details. Use your browser’s back button to return to the report from the contact.

Invoice

This column lists the bill invoice number for the matter. In the Web report, you can click on the invoice number to view invoice details. Use your browser’s back button to return to the report from the invoice.

Practice area

This column shows the practice area for the matter. If a practice area was not selected, this column will be blank.

Responsible attorney

This column shows the responsible attorney assigned to the matter.

Originating attorney

This column shows the originating attorney assigned to the matter.

Billed hours

This column shows the total hours that a firm user spent on the activities on a bill that is approved but unpaid or a bill that has been paid. This information is pulled directly from the listed bill invoice. Credit notes and write-offs will not affect the number of billed hours but discounts will affect the number of billed hours.

Billed time

This column shows the dollar value of the time entries a specific firm user generated on a bill that is approved but unpaid or a bill that has been paid. This information is pulled directly from the listed bill invoice. Credit notes and write-offs will not affect billed time but discounts will affect billed time.

Billed time allocation

This column refers to the percentage of billed time on a bill that a user is responsible for. If multiple firm users have time entries on a single bill, this column will show the percentage of time that each user is responsible for.

Collected time

This columns shows the dollar value of the time entries on bills that have been paid.

Outstanding time

This column shows the dollar value of the time entries on bills that are approved but have not been paid.

Billed expense

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the dollar value of the expenses a specific firm user generated on a bill that is approved but unpaid or a bill that has been paid.

Expense allocation

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the percentage of billed expenses on a bill that a user is responsible for. If multiple firm users have expense entries on a single bill, this column will show the percentage of expenses that each user is responsible for.

Collected expense

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the dollar value of the expense entries on bills that have been paid.

Outstanding expense

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the dollar value of the expense entries on bills that are approved but have not been paid.

Total collected

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It is the total amount of payments applied to specific bills.

Total outstanding

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It is the total amount of unpaid time and expenses on specific bills.

Interest collected

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the total dollar value of the interest on bills that have been paid.

Interest outstanding

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the total dollar value of the interest on bills that are approved but have not been paid.

Collected tax 1

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the total dollar value of the primary tax on bills that have been paid.

Outstanding tax 1

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the total dollar value of the primary tax on bills that are approved but have not been paid.

Collected tax 2

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the total dollar value of the secondary tax on bills that have been paid.

Outstanding tax 2

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the total dollar value of the secondary tax on bills that are approved but have not been paid.

Collected time allocated to responsible attorney

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the total dollar value of collected time to allocate to the responsible attorney.

Collected time allocated to originating attorney

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the total dollar value of collected time to allocate to the originating attorney.

Matter billing method

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the billing method selected on the matter, with options for contingency, flat fee, or hourly.

Non-billable time amount

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. It shows the dollar value of the non-billable time entries a specific firm user generated for that matter.

Non-billable time allocation

This column will only appear if this report is generated in CSV format. This column refers to the percentage of non-billable time on a matter that a firm user is responsible for.

  • Billed information will be included if the bill issue date for that entry falls within the date range selected when generating the report.
  • Collected amounts and information will be included if the payment date falls within the date range selected when generating the report.

results.title: Migrating Data From Your Current Software [T-Z]
results.body:
This article explains what data can be migrated from your current practice management software and how to export the data from that software. Software applications starting with the letters T, U, W, and Z, and any numbers are listed below.

Tip: See one of the articles below if your current practice management software does not start with the letters T, U, W, Z, or any numbers.

  • Migrating Data From Your Current Software [A-B]
  • Migrating Data From Your Current Software [C-F]
  • Migrating Data From Your Current Software [G-M]
  • Migrating Data From Your Current Software [N-S]

 

Tabs3/PracticeMaster

What can I migrate? How do I migrate my data?
  • Contacts
  • Matters
  • Unbilled Expenses Entries
  • Unbilled Time Entries
  • Matter Notes
  • Calendar Events
  • Tasks
  • Email Communications
  • Phone Communications
  • Outstanding Balances (a single line item that represents the summative balance at time of export for a Matter)
  • Trust Balances (a single line item that represents the summative balance at time of export for a Matter or Contact)

Note: Depending on the quality of your data, we may also be able to migrate email and phone communications, contact and matter notes, calendar events, tasks, and unbilled time and expense entries.

Note: Tabs3 does not have an export function. Your data can only be exported through the PracticeMaster interface. The PracticeMaster version should be compatible with the Tabs3 version to synchronize properly. If you are having issues with setting up PracticeMaster or have sync issues, contact Tabs3 support to set up PracticeMaster.

Contacts, matters, and other files:

  1. Select the Maintenance tab and click File Maintenance.

  2. Select the desired Export Files.

  3. Click OK.
  4. Select Utility and click Export Data.
  5. Rename the file and add .csv to convert it into a spreadsheet format.
  6. Click Ok.

 

Timekeeper list (with ID numbers):

  1. Go to the TABS module.
  2. Click Reports > Miscellaneous > Timekeepers List.
  3. Export file to XLSX format.

 

Category list (with ID numbers and for practice areas):

  1. Go to the TABS module.
  2. Click Reports > Miscellaneous > Category List.
  3. Export file to XLSX format.

 

Task code list (with ID numbers):

  1. Go to the TABS module.
  2. Click Reports > Miscellaneous > Task Code List
  3. Export file to XLSX format.

 

Transaction code list (with ID numbers):

Note: The Tcode column in CMFEE and CMCOST will migrate to the activity categories for time and expenses in Clio.

  1. Go to the TABS module.
  2. Click Reports > Miscellaneous > Transaction Code List.
  3. Export file to XLSX format.

 

Accounts receivables:

  1. Go to Reports > Accounts Receivable > AR Summary Report.
  2. Select Sort tab settings.
  3. Check Subtotal by Client.
  4. Select Report Order = None.
  5. Click OK to generate the report and then export as Excel format (e.g. xlsx, csv, etc.).

 

Trust balances:

  1. Go to the TAS (Trust Accounting Software) module on the bottom left of the PM.
  2. Click Reports.
  3. Select Trust Account List Report and save the data in xlsx format.

 

Thryv

What can I migrate? How do I migrate my data?
  • Contacts
  • Calendar Events

Contacts:

  1. Go to Clients on the left side panel.
  2. Optional: Click Filter and set parameters as needed.
  3. Click More actions in the top right and select Export from the dropdown menu.
  4. In the new modal, under Rows, if you previously set filters, click Filtered.
  5. Under Format, select CSV if not already selected.
  6. Click Download.

 

Calendar:

  1. Go to Calendar on the left side panel.
  2. Optional: Click Filter and set appropriate filters.
  3. Click More actions in the top right and select Export booking data from the dropdown menu.
  4. In the Appointments and Events Reports modal, confirm or set a date range.
  5. Under Columns, select All.
  6. Under Rows, if you previously set filters, click Custom.
  7. Under Format, select CSV or Excel.
  8. Click Download.

 

Time & Chaos

What can I migrate? How do I migrate my data?
  • Contacts
  • Matters (limited information from v. 10.2)
  • Tasks
  • Unbilled Time Entries (v. 10.2)
  • Unbilled Expense Entries (v. 10.2)
  • Calendar Events

Note: We have not confirmed the exact nature of what can be migrated from this program to Clio. You can, however, still follow the export directions.

  1. Click Reports and select Contacts.
  2. Right click on any of the columns to show a list of available fields. Select the fields you want included in the export.
  3. Click Find Now.
  4. Select all items.
  5. Click File and select Export to Excel.
  6. Repeat the above steps for Calendar and Tasks.

 

Time Matters

What can I migrate? How do I migrate my data?
  • Contacts
  • Matters
  • Notes
  • Related Contacts
  • Tasks (To-dos)
  • Calendar Events
  • Phone Communications
  • Email Communications
  • Unbilled Time Entries
  • Unbilled Expense Entries
  • Outstanding Balances (a single line item that represents the summative balance at time of export for a Matter)

Note: Depending on the quality of the data, we may be able to migrate email and phone communications and outstanding balances.

Database Backup

Note: Clio requires only the SQL database backup, which uses the default naming convention "TimeMattersAutomatedBackup[Day].bak". Find this file in the default backup location for the Microsoft SQL Server. Time Matters SQL database backups are stored in a different location than Time Matters document and email file backups, which are backed up to the Server. The default location for SQL backup data is C:\Program Files\Microsoft SQL Server\MSSQL.XX\MSSQL\Backup or C:\Program Files(x86)\Microsoft SQL Server\MSSQL.XX\MSSQL\Backup.

  1. Open Time Matters.
  2. Go to File > Backup Time Matters Data.
  3. Verify that the Shared Files Backup location is correct.
  4. Optional: Click the ellipsis menu to change the location where the shared files will be saved.
  5. Check the box next to Skip files in the Documents and Documents Index Directories.
  6. Check the box next to Skip backing up of email attachments.
  7. To keep a non-default Shared Files Backup location for future backups, check the box next to Remember this destination for future backups.
  8. Select Backup Now, if available.
  9. Click OK to start the backup process.

Important: If an error occurs while creating the backup, retrieve the backup from Microsoft SQL Server directly. Consult your IT team about the best way to create this file. For a Clio data migration, provide only the appropriate .bak file from the [...]MSSQL\Backup folder noted above.

 

Front-end reports

Step 1: Follow these initial steps to get started.

  1. Open Time Matters.
  2. Go to File > Setup > User and Security > Security Settings.
  3. Uncheck the box for Activate Security Features Throughout the Application (Recommended).
  4. Recheck the box once the export is completed.

Step 2: Export your data. See the sections below.

Important: When doing a typical Time Matters migration, only the Contacts and Matters front-end reports are exported along with the Time Matters database backup. Additionally, only export the remaining sections as a workaround if you are unable to export a Time Matters database backup.

Contacts:

  1. Open Time Matters.
  2. Go to File > Export > Custom Export.
  3. Select Create a new Export Template.
  4. Click Next.
  5. On the Select Export File Format page, select ASCII - Comma Delimited (.TXT or .CSV) > check Include field names labels as first record in Export > click “...” > assign the file a name and select a location, typically in c:\Clio Export\ (creating the folder Clio Export).
  6. On the Specify Time Matter Record Type page, select the Export the following Record Type dropdown menu and choose Contacts.
  7. On the Select Pre-Merge Record page, select None > click Next.
  8. On the Export Custom Forms page, select None > click Next.
  9. On the Select Contact Export Fields page, click Add All > remove the Memo field from the selection > click Next > when it asks about Archived Status, make sure to get BOTH non-archived data and archived data (unless preferences are otherwise).
  10. On the Launch Application After Export page, select No, do not launch an application > click Next.
  11. On the Ready to Begin Export page, select Yes. Save this Export Template > click Finish.
  12. When the export is complete, click OK.

 

Matters:

  1. Open Time Matters.
  2. Go to File > Export > Custom Export.
  3. Select Create a new Export Template.
  4. Click Next.
  5. On the Select Export File Format page, select ASCII - Comma Delimited (.TXT or .CSV) > check Include field names labels as first record in Export > click “...” > assign the file a name and select a location, typically in c:\Clio Export\ (creating the folder Clio Export).
  6. On the Specify Time Matter Record Type page, select the Export the following Record Type dropdown menu and choose Cases.
  7. On the Select Pre-Merge Record page, select None > click Next.
  8. On the Export Custom Forms page, select None > click Next.
  9. On the Select Matter Export Fields page, click Add All > remove the Memo field from the selection > click Next (filter and export by practice area to get header names) > when it asks about Archived Status, make sure to get BOTH non-archived data and archived data (unless preferences are otherwise).
  10. On the Launch Application After Export page, select No, do not launch an application > click Next.
  11. On the Ready to Begin Export page, select Yes. Save this Export Template > click Finish.
  12. When the export is complete, click OK.

 

Calendar events:

  1. Open Time Matters.
  2. Go to File > Export > Custom Export.
  3. Select Create a new Export Template.
  4. Click Next.
  5. On the Select Export File Format page, select ASCII - Comma Delimited (.TXT or .CSV) > check Include field names labels as first record in Export > click “...” > assign the file a name and select a location, typically in c:\Clio Export\ (creating the folder Clio Export).
  6. On the Specify Time Matter Record Type page, select the Export the following Record Type dropdown menu and choose Events.
  7. On the Select Pre-Merge Record page, select None > click Next.
  8. On the Export Custom Forms page, select None > click Next.
  9. On the Select Matter Export Fields page, click Add All > remove the Memo field from the selection > click Next > when it asks about Archived Status, make sure to get BOTH non-archived data and archived data (unless preferences are otherwise).
  10. On the Launch Application After Export page, select No, do not launch an application > click Next.
  11. On the Ready to Begin Export page, select Yes. Save this Export Template > click Finish.
  12. When the export is complete, click OK.

 

Tasks:

  1. Open Time Matters.
  2. Go to File > Export > Custom Export.
  3. Select Create a new Export Template.
  4. Click Next.
  5. On the Select Export File Format page, select ASCII - Comma Delimited (.TXT or .CSV) > check Include field names labels as first record in Export > click “...” > assign the file a name and select a location, typically in c:\Clio Export\ (creating the folder Clio Export).
  6. On the Specify Time Matter Record Type page, select the Export the following Record Type dropdown menu and choose To Dos.
  7. On the Select Pre-Merge Record page, select None > click Next.
  8. On the Export Custom Forms page, select None > click Next.
  9. On the Select Matter Export Fields page, click Add All > remove the Memo field from the selection > click Next > when it asks about Archived Status, make sure to get BOTH non-archived data and archived data (unless preferences are otherwise).
  10. On the Launch Application After Export page, select No, do not launch an application > click Next.
  11. On the Ready to Begin Export page, select Yes. Save this Export Template > click Finish.
  12. When the export is complete, click OK.

 

Notes:

  1. Open Time Matters.
  2. Go to File > Export > Custom Export.
  3. Select Create a new Export Template.
  4. Click Next.
  5. On the Select Export File Format page, select ASCII - Comma Delimited (.TXT or .CSV) > check Include field names labels as first record in Export > click “...” > assign the file a name and select a location, typically in c:\Clio Export\ (creating the folder Clio Export).
  6. On the Specify Time Matter Record Type page, select the Export the following Record Type dropdown menu and choose Notes.
  7. On the Select Pre-Merge Record page, select None > click Next.
  8. On the Export Custom Forms page, select None > click Next.
  9. On the Select Matter Export Fields page, click Add All > remove the Memo field from the selection > click Next > when it asks about Archived Status, make sure to get BOTH non-archived data and archived data (unless preferences are otherwise).
  10. On the Launch Application After Export page, select No, do not launch an application > click Next.
  11. On the Ready to Begin Export page, select Yes. Save this Export Template > click Finish.
  12. When the export is complete, click OK.

 

Time and expenses:

  1. Open Time Matters.
  2. Go to File > Export > Custom Export.
  3. Select Create a new Export Template.
  4. Click Next.
  5. On the Select Export File Format page, select ASCII - Comma Delimited (.TXT or .CSV) > check Include field names labels as first record in Export > click “...” > assign the file a name and select a location, typically in c:\Clio Export\ (creating the folder Clio Export).
  6. On the Specify Time Matter Record Type page, select the Export the following Record Type dropdown menu and choose Billing.
  7. On the Select Pre-Merge Record page, select None > click Next.
  8. On the Export Custom Forms page, select None > click Next.
  9. On the Select Matter Export Fields page, click Add All > remove the Memo field from the selection > click Next > when it asks about Archived Status, make sure to get BOTH non-archived data and archived data (unless preferences are otherwise).
  10. On the Launch Application After Export page, select No, do not launch an application > click Next.
  11. On the Ready to Begin Export page, select Yes. Save this Export Template > click Finish.
  12. When the export is complete, click OK.

 

Time59

What can I migrate? How do I migrate my data?
  • Contacts
  • Matters (derived from contact listing)
  • Unbilled time and expense entries

Contacts:

  1. Click on export in the main menu.
  2. Select Export to Excel.
  3. Select Clients from the dropdown.
  4. Select All or the date range for the data.
  5. Click Export.

 

Time entries:

Note: If time entry exports are too large, the file may become corrupted. Time entry data may have to be exported in smaller batches.

  1. Click on export in the main menu.
  2. Select Export to Excel.
  3. Select Time from the dropdown.
  4. Select All or the date range for the data.
  5. Click Export.

 

Expense entries:

  1. Click on export in the main menu.
  2. Select Export to Excel.
  3. Select Expenses from the dropdown.
  4. Select All or the date range for the data.
  5. Click Export.

 

TimeSlips

What can I migrate? How do I migrate my data?
  • Contacts
  • Matters (derived from the client list)
  • Unbilled Time Entries
  • Unbilled Expense Entries
  • Outstanding balances (a single line item that represents the summative balance at time of export for a matter)

  • Trust Balances (a single line item that represents the balance at time of export for a matter or contact)

     

Note: You can only export from TimeSlips if you are operating a version of a program from 2006 or later.

Contacts and matters:

  1. Click Reports > Clients.
  2. Click the + sign in the top right of the dialogue box.
  3. Click Add a specific standard report to the report list.
  4. Select the Client Info Listing report and then click Next.
  5. Click Next.
  6. Click Open Report Entry and then click Next.
  7. Double click Client Classification and filter for open, closed, or inactive records as needed.
  8. Click Options and confirm that all the boxes are checked.
  9. Click Print to, select Microsoft Excel File and then click Print.
  10. Check the box for Include column titles and then click OK.
    • The excel file will automatically open after the export. Once opened, save the file in .xls format.

 

Unbilled time and expense entries:

  1. Click Reports.
  2. Click the + sign in the top right of the dialogue box.
  3. Click Add a specific standard report to the report list.
  4. Select the Slip Listing report and then click Next.
  5. Click Next.
  6. Click Open Report Entry and then click Next.
  7. Select Slips from Filter Groups.
  8. Double click Slip Billed and set it to No.

TrialWorks

What can I migrate? How do I migrate my data?
Note: Data types with an asterisk (*) require a backup from TrialWorks and are subject to review for data quality. See Option 1 under "How do I migrate my data?" for more information.
  • Contacts
  • Matters

  • Matter Notes*

There are two methods for exporting data from Trial Works: by requesting a backup from their database and accessing the backup using Microsoft SQL Server Management Studio Express (option 1), or by exporting using their reports functionality to export contacts, clients, and matters (option 2).

Option 1

Step 1: Contact TrialWorks to request a backup of the TrialWorks database.

Step 2: Follow these steps to access the data in your backup:

  1. Open SQL Server Management Studio Express and connect to the SQL server.
  2. Expand Databases.
  3. Right-click on the database you want to back up, and then select Tasks > Back up (this is not available for version 2018/2019).
  4. On the Back Up Database window, make sure the Database field contains the name of the database you want to back up.
  5. Select Full for the Backup Type.
  6. Click Remove to remove the default/last backup file name.
  7. Click Add to open the Select Backup Destination window.
  8. Click [...] next to the File Name field.
  9. On the Locate Database Files window, select the folder where you want the backup file to go. By default, it is ..\Microsoft SQL Server\MSSQL.1\MSSQL\Backup.
  10. In the File Name field, type the name for this backup, with a .bak extension. For example,xyz_20080221.bak for a backup of the XYZ database created on 21 February 2008.
  11. Click OK to close the Locate Database Files window.
  12. Click OK to close the Select Backup Destination window.
  13. Click OK to start the backup. The progress icon displays in the lower-left corner, and a completed successfully message displays when it is done.

 

Option 2

Export contacts:

  1. Click Reports in the menu bar and select Report Writer to open the Custom Report Export window.
  2. Click Edit Queries…
  3. In the Query/Filter Name enter an export name. E.g. Clio Export Contacts.
  4. Select Contacts Table for the Table Name.
  5. Add a new row for each field you want to include in the report:
    • Select the FieldName that you would like included in the export.

  4. Select Clients Table for the Table Name.
  5. Add a new row for each field you want to include in the report:
    • Select the FieldName that you would like included in the export.
    • Select SHOW for the Condition.
  6. Click the Exit.
  7. In the Export Format, select Excel and click Export. Save the file when the report opens in Excel.

 

Export matters:

  1. Click Reports in the menu bar and select Report Writer to open the Custom Report Export window.
  2. Click Edit Queries…
  3. In the Query/Filter Name enter an export name. E.g. Clio Export Matters.
  4. Select Matters Table for the Table Name.
  5. Add a new row for each field you want to include in the report:
    • Select the FieldName that you would like included in the export.
    • Select SHOW for the Condition.
  6. Click the Exit.
  7. In the Export Format, select Excel and click Export. Save the file when the report opens in Excel.

results.title: Clio Grow Reports
results.body:
Reports in Clio Grow are designed around common data needs of firms. Each report allows you to filter data based on specific parameters to meet your needs.

 

Matter revenue report

The Matter Revenue Report in Clio Grow provides a detailed overview about revenue for different lead sources, campaigns, and referrals, matter status, categories, and types.

If you use both Clio Grow and Clio Manage, this report shows contact and matter details from both Clio Grow and Clio Manage, helping you track where your firm's profit originates and identify value sources. Make sure to convert relevant matters from Grow to Manage, and make sure that your contacts between Grow and Manage are synced. While contacts typically sync automatically, you can also sync contacts manually when necessary. If a matter exists only in Clio Grow, the report will not display any associated Clio Manage fields.

You can also generate a matter revenue report from Clio Manage.

Note: The data from Clio Grow used for this report refreshes when the report is generated or when new filters are applied. Data from Clio Manage refreshes at intervals and the time of the last refresh will appear in a note at the top of the report.

To generate this report:

  1. Go to Reports.
  2. Click Matter revenue report.
    • To generate this report, first enable shared contacts.
  3. Set all report filter parameters as necessary.

  4. Click View report.

    • Optional: Click Columns to adjust the columns included in the report, and Update columns to apply the changes.
    • Optional: Click Filters to adjust the filters used to generate the report, then click Apply filters to apply the changes
    • Contacts and matters have clickable links in case you want to quickly refer to specific contact or matter details.

    Note: Click Download CSV to use this report outside of Clio Grow. The download will include all previously selected columns and pages.

This report includes the following data:

Contact data
Contact

This column shows the contact associated with each matter. It is sorted alphabetically by first name. You can click on any contact name to open a new tab with the contact's details. Learn more about Clio Grow contacts here.

Email

This column displays the primary email address entered when a contact was created.

Referred by

This column shows the referral source if another contact referred the prospective client.

Source data
First touch

This column shows the first marketing source that brought the prospective client to your firm (if any).

Provider

This column shows the connected integration or app, or the Clio-built feature, that created the record (e.g., Zapier, Grow AI).

Campaign

This column shows the marketing campaign associated with the matter's source (if any).

Clio Grow data
Matter

This column lists the name of the matter in Clio Grow. You can click on the matter to open a new tab in Clio Grow with the matter details.

Description

This column displays the information entered in the Description field when the matter was created.

Matter type

This column shows the type of matter, similar to Clio Manage practice areas.

Matter status - top level

This column displays the current top-level status of the matter within the pipeline. Learn more about matter statuses here.

Matter status - detailed

This column displays the stage of the matter within the pipeline’s status.

Status date

This column shows the date the matter status was last updated.

Created at

This column shows the date when the matter was created.

Location

This column displays information from the Location field when the matter was created.

Estimated value

This column displays the anticipated total legal fees to be earned, as entered when the matter was created.

Clio Manage data
Matter

This column lists the name of the matter in Clio Manage. You can click on the matter to open a new tab in Clio Manage with the matter details. 

Description

This column displays the information entered in the Description field when the matter was created in Clio Manage.

Practice area

This column displays the practice area associated with the matter.

Matter status

This column shows the current status of the matter (Open, Pending, or Closed).

Status date

This column shows the date when the matter status was last updated.

Created at

This column shows the date the matter was created in Clio Manage.

Location

This column displays the information entered in the Location field when the matter was created.

Originating attorney

This column lists the firm user selected as the originating attorney for the matter. If no originating attorney was selected, this field will be blank.

Responsible attorney

This column lists the firm user currently responsible for the matter. If no responsible attorney is selected, this field will be blank.

Revenue data
Unbilled time

This column shows the total unbilled time for each matter and includes time entries on bills in draft or bills pending approval

Unbilled hours

This column shows the unbilled time entry hours for each matter. Unbilled time includes time entries not on approved bills, including those on bills in draft or pending approval.

Unbilled expenses

This column displays the total unbilled expenses for each matter. Unbilled activities are those on bills in draft or bills pending approval.

Billed time

This column displays the total value of billed time entries for the matter. Billed time entries are those that appear on approved bills.

Billed hours

This column shows the number of billed hours for the matter. Billed hours are time entries on approved bills.

Billed expenses

This column shows the dollar value of billed expense entries for the matter. Billed expense entries are those on approved bills.

Collected time

This column displays the dollar value of billed time entries for which payments have been received.

Collected expenses

This column displays the dollar value of billed expenses for which payments have been received.

Revenue

This column shows the total revenue for each matter, calculated by subtracting expenses from billable amounts.

 

Lead source revenue report

The lead source revenue report is designed to give firms a summary of the leads generated by different types of advertising or outreach and the business generated from the advertising or outreach. This report also shows estimated matter values across lead sources. You can use this report to understand the revenue driven from your marketing and referral sources.

If you use both Clio Grow and Clio Manage, this report uses information from both Clio Grow and Clio Manage.

Note: The data from Clio Grow used for this report refreshes when the report is generated or when new filters are applied. Data from Clio Manage refreshes at intervals and the time of the last refresh will appear in a note at the top of the report.

To generate this report:

  1. Go to Reports.
  2. Select Lead source revenue report.
  3. Set all report filter parameters as necessary.
  4. Click View report.
    • Optional: Click Columns to adjust the columns included in the report, and Update columns to apply the changes.
    • Optional: Click Filters to adjust the filters used to generate the report, then click Apply filters to apply the changes.
Source

This column shows the source of a prospective client and will be Unassigned if no lead source is assigned.

Intake matters

Total number of intakes generated for each lead source. When you click on the number in a particular lead Source row, a Matter revenue report will open in a new tab with the filters associated with the number you clicked (i.e., the original filters used to create the Lead source revenue report, a value of Intake applied to the Matter Status - top-level filter, and the applicable lead source from the row of the number you clicked applied to the Source filter).

Hired matters

Total number of hires generated for each lead source. When you click on the number in a particular lead Source row, a Matter revenue report will open in a new tab with the filters associated with the number you clicked (i.e., the original filters used to create the Lead source revenue report, a value of Hired applied to the Matter Status - top-level filter, and the applicable lead source from the row of the number you clicked applied to the Source filter).

Not hired matters

Total number of intakes that were not hired for each lead source. When you click on the number in a particular lead Source row, a Matter revenue report will open in a new tab with the filters associated with the number you clicked (i.e., the original filters used to create the Lead source revenue report, a value of Not hired applied to the Matter Status - top-level filter, and the applicable lead source from the row of the number you clicked applied to the Source filter).

Hired conversion rate

The percentage of hires from the total number of intakes by lead source.

Estimated value

This column is calculated from the amount entered in the Value field when creating a matter in Clio Grow and is a total from all matters.

Revenue

This column shows the total revenue earned from the lead source. The number is pulled from the billable profit of the activities in Clio Manage.

Spend

For firms in the US advertising on Google’s Local Services Ads, this column shows the amount your firm is spending on the campaign.

ROI (as a multiplier)

For firms in the US advertising on Google’s Local Services Ads, this shows the revenue earned divided by the amount spent on ads.

ROI (as a percentage)

For firms in the US advertising on Google’s Local Services Ads, this shows the revenue earned divided by the amount spent on ads expressed as a percentage.

Matters added report

The matters added report shows a visual overview of matters added to your pipeline including the lead source, the pipeline value, and the rate at which your firm is converting leads to clients (i.e., the Conversion rate). You can view your data as bar, line, or pie chart, and group results by lead source or matter type.

To generate this report:

  1. Go to Reports.
  2. Select Matters added report.
  3. Optional: Click Apply Filters to adjust the data according to your needs, then click Generate Report to apply the changes to the report.

When generated, this report includes the following data:

Matters added

This refers to the number of leads or matters that have been added to the account within a given period of time. It is broken down by lead source and matter type. The report provides a visual representation, in either graph or table format, of which lead sources and matter types are generating the greatest number of cases.

Pipeline value

This chart displays the estimated value of matters in the pipeline by lead source or matter type over a given period. You can review this report in graph or table format.

Conversion rate

This chart shows the total number of hired matters divided by the total number of all matters added in a specific time period broken down by lead source and matter type.

Note: You can download the data by changing your View to table (click the Table icon), clicking then Download CSV.

 

Referral report

The referral report in Clio Grow lists the contacts who refer clients to your firm and the total number of matters, summarizing which referral sources brought in potential clients and the types of matters they referred.

  1. Go to Reports.
  2. Select Referral report.
    • Optional: Click Apply Filters to restrict data. You can change the date range and select or deselect matter types, lead sources, or users. Click Generate Report to apply the filters.
    • Optional: Click Download CSV to save the data outside of Clio Grow.

When generated, this report includes the following data:

Name

This column shows the name of the referral contact, as entered in the Referred by field when creating a contact.

Total Referrals

This column shows the total number of referrals made by the contact.

Total Matters

This column shows the number of matters referred to your firm by this contact.

Intake

This column shows the number of matters referred to your firm from this contact with an Intake matter status in the Pipeline. Learn more about matter statuses here (include link)

Hired

This column shows the number of referrals from this contact that resulted in the firm being hired.

Did Not Hire

This column shows the number of referrals where the client chose not to hire your firm.

Total Value

This column shows the combined total of the Value fields for all matters referred to your firm by the contact.

Average Value

This column shows the average value of matters referred by the contact.

Intake Value

This column shows the total value of matters referred by the contact with an Intake status.

Hired Value

This column shows the total value of matters referred by the contact with an Intake status.

Did Not Hire Value

This column shows the total value of matters where the client did not hire your firm.

Conversion Rate %

This column shows the percentage of referred matters that resulted in your firm being hired, calculated by dividing hired matters by the total number of referred matters.

results.body:
Reports in Clio Manage are designed to help your law firm track deliverables and get insights into all aspects of how the firm is performing. Matter reports provide a comprehensive overview of matter listings, matters by responsible attorney, contact listing, and billing rate. See below for a summary of each matter report in Clio Manage and what type of information the report offers.

Note: Every report in Clio is unique in the criteria it uses to calculate financial data. This means that comparing reports is not recommended. Additionally, not all reports are available for all Clio subscription plans. Learn more about reports available on your subscription plan and upgrading your plan here.
Tip: Learn more about generating reports, creating reports presets, and viewing a history of generated reports here.

Matters report

The matters report is designed to give firms a detailed view of clients and matters. This report includes matter description, responsible attorney, originating attorney, last bill date, accounts receivable, whether the matter is billable, practice area, status of the matter, and the client’s name. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Client

This column lists the name of the client attached to the matter and is sorted alphabetically by client last name.

Matter

This column lists each of a client's matters.

Description

This column shows the information entered in the Description field when a matter was created.

Practice area

This column shows the practice area for the matter. If a practice area was not selected, this column will be blank.

Status

This column shows the matter's current status. A matter can either be Open, Pending, or Closed. 

Responsible attorney

This column shows the firm user currently responsible for the matter.

Originating attorney

This column shows the firm user that was selected as the originating attorney on the matter.

Billable

This column shows whether the matter is billable or non-billable.

Accounts receivable

This column shows the amount currently owed on an outstanding bill. This column will only show approved bills that have not been paid.

Latest bill

This column shows the date that the last bill was generated.

 

Matters by responsible attorney report

The matters by responsible attorney report is designed to give firms a quick view of matters grouped by responsible attorney. This report includes the client’s name and matter description. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Matter

This column lists each of a client's matters.

Client

This column lists the name of the client attached to the matter. If a client was deleted or reassigned from a matter, you will see a blank space under this column. Clients are sorted alphabetically by client last name for each responsible attorney.

Description

This column shows the information entered in the Description field when a matter was created.

No assigned responsible attorney

This section appears below all of the matters with responsible attorneys and shows matters and clients that do not have an assigned responsible attorney.

 

Contact information report

The contact information report is designed to give firms a quick view of clients, their matters, and basic contact information. You can use this report to generate an email list. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Client name

This column lists the name of the client attached to a matter. If a client has more than one matter, you will see their name listed again for each matter.

Matter

This column lists each of a client's matters.

Primary phone number

This column shows the client's first phone number or the phone number that is designated as the primary phone number.

Primary email address

This column shows the client's first email address or the email address that is designated as the primary email address.

 

Billing rate report

The billing rate report is designed to give firms an overview of custom billing rates for all matters. It shows matters, users, and the current client, matter, and user default billing rates. This report helps you identify which clients, staff, or practice areas bring in the most revenue and provides insight into the accuracy and effectiveness of your firm's billing rates. When generated, this report includes the following categories:

Client

This column lists clients with matters that have time and expense entries on file and is sorted alphabetically by client first name. Clients with multiple matters will appear multiple times.

Matter number

This column lists each of a client's matters and shows the matter number.

Matter description

This column shows the information entered in the Description field when a matter was created.

User

This column shows the name of the firm user whose billing rate is applied to the matter. 

Practice area

This column shows the practice area selected when the matter was created. If no practice area was selected, this column will be blank.

Rate type

This column shows the rate type that you selected before generating the report. Selecting Default and custom rates will show user, client, and matter rates. Selecting Custom matter rates only will show only matter rates. Selecting Custom client rates only will show only client rates. Selecting Custom matter and client rates only will show the matter and client rates, but not the user's default rate.

Each client row in the export will show the billing rate that the matter is using and is contingent on rate hierarchy. The rate hierarchy is as follows: User Matter Rate > User Client Rate > User Default Rate.
